name: Cold Email Variant Tester with Deliverability Score

parameters.content:
## Cold Email Variant Tester with Deliverability Score

Most cold email templates write one email and send it. This one writes three
different angles, scores each against the rules that decide whether cold email
lands and gets read, saves the winner as a Gmail draft for a human to approve,
and queues the follow up. Nothing is sent without you.

### How it works

A form collects the prospect, your reason for writing now, and your own sender
details, so the template is not hard-wired to one agency. The contact email is
checked against your Outreach tab first: a prospect already in the sequence
stops here with a notice, so nobody is mailed twice. The writer then produces
three variants on deliberately different angles plus a follow up. Each variant
is scored in code, not by the model: subject length, spam trigger words, worn
out openers, body length, link count, whether the first name and company
actually appear, whether there is a question to reply to, and whether any
placeholder was left unfilled. Every deduction is recorded in plain English.
The best variant becomes a Gmail draft. A variant under seventy is drafted too,
but with a review prefix and its problem list attached, so weak copy is visible
instead of sent. Both steps are written to the sheet with a send date, which
turns the sheet into the sequence. The form then shows all three scores.

### Setup

Connect Gmail, Sheets and your model credentials, set your sheet ID, and create
the Outreach tab with the columns named on the suppression node.

### Customization

Four optional nodes sit unconnected below the canvas. Plug in the ones you
want: send without review, Slack notifications, live website enrichment, or
calendar reminders. Each one carries a note saying where it goes.

## Prospect in, duplicates out
The form takes the prospect and your own sender details. A contact already in the Outreach tab stops here, so nobody is mailed twice.

## Three angles, not one email
The writer returns three variants on deliberately different angles, plus a follow up for four business days later. Gemini stands in if the main model fails.

## Score them, then pick
Subject length, spam words, tired openers, link count, personalisation and leftover placeholders are all scored in code. The best variant wins and every deduction is named.

## Draft, queue, confirm
The winner becomes a Gmail draft. Weak copy is drafted with a review prefix and its problem list. Both steps are written to the sheet with a send date.

options.systemMessage:
You write first touch cold emails that a busy person would actually reply to.

Produce three variants of the same email, each taking a genuinely different angle:
1. A specific observation about the prospect's business, and what it implies.
2. A relevant result or approach, described without naming other clients.
3. A direct, short note that simply asks whether the problem is worth a conversation.

Rules for every variant
- Open on the prospect, never on the sender. The first sentence must be about them.
- Use the contact's first name only, and name their company at least once.
- 60 to 130 words of body text. Short paragraphs wrapped in p tags.
- Exactly one call to action, and phrase it as a question so replying is easy.
- At most one link.
- No emoji, no exclamation marks, no capitalised words.
- Never write: I hope this email finds you, I wanted to reach out, quick question, just checking in, game changer, unlock, revolutionary, guaranteed.
- Never invent statistics, client names, case study numbers, funding rounds or news. Use only what the brief gives you.
- Leave no placeholder brackets of any kind in the text.
- Close with the sender name and company from the brief.

Also write one follow up email for four business days later: under 70 words, referencing the first note without repeating it, and ending in an easier question than the first.

Give each variant a short angle label. Return only the requested JSON fields.
